short: The call to prayer.
Weak: the grading for a hadith that falls short of the conditions for acceptance.
Remembering Allah, especially by repeating set words of praise.
Asking Allah, in any words, for anything.
Obligatory: an act that must be done.
Islamic law as scholars understand it from its sources.
A wash of the whole body that restores purity after certain states.
A report of what the Prophet ﷺ said, did or approved.
The pilgrimage to Makkah, made in the month of Dhu al-Hijjah.
Permitted.
Forbidden.
Good: a grading just below sahih. Such a hadith is still accepted as evidence.
A full lunar year of holding wealth at or above the nisab.
Breaking the fast at sunset.
Consensus: the agreement of the scholars on a ruling.
The second call, said just before the prayer begins.
The chain of narrators through whom a hadith reached us.
Asking Allah for forgiveness.
Friday, and the congregational prayer held at midday on it.
The House in Makkah that Muslims face in prayer.
A sermon, as given before the Friday prayer.
A school of law. Here: the Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi’i and Hanbali schools.
Disliked: better left undone.
The wording of a hadith, after its chain.
A report that stops at a Companion and is not traced back to the Prophet ﷺ.
A report in which a Successor quotes the Prophet ﷺ without naming the Companion in between.
Recommended: rewarded if done, no blame if left.
The minimum amount of wealth on which zakat falls due.
Intention: the purpose in the heart behind an act.
Making up a prayer or fast later.
The direction of the Kaaba in Makkah, which Muslims face in prayer.
One cycle of the prayer: standing, bowing and two prostrations.
Bowing in prayer, hands on the knees.
A Companion: someone who met the Prophet ﷺ as a believer and died a Muslim.
Sound: the grading for a hadith whose chain and wording meet the strictest conditions.
The prayer: the five daily prayers, and other prayers, performed in set positions.
Fasting: no food, drink or intercourse from dawn until sunset.
The meal before dawn on a fasting day.
Prostration: forehead, nose, hands, knees and toes on the ground.
The Prophet’s way: what he ﷺ said, did and approved.
A Successor: a Muslim of the generation that met the Companions.
Purity: the state needed for prayer, and the ways of reaching it.
Saying la ilaha illa Allah, “there is no god but Allah”.
Saying al-hamdu lillah, “praise be to Allah”.
Saying Allahu akbar, “Allah is greatest”.
Saying subhan Allah, “glory be to Allah”. Also used for counting dhikr.
The words of witness said while sitting in the prayer.
Purifying with clean earth when water can’t be used.
The lesser pilgrimage, which can be made at any time of year.
Obligatory. In the Hanafi school, a level just below fard.
Washing set parts of the body to be ready for prayer.
The yearly due on wealth above a set minimum, given to those entitled to receive it.
